0.gpu_models: RTX 3050 A 4 GB; YOLO detected 4 people; SmolVLM captioned image on CUDA; measurements in docs/gpu-smoke.md

1.chat: eval.test_chatbot on 200 synthetic events: 20/20 saved questions matched expected rows; DROP, UPDATE, and DELETE all rejected; fixture intact.
1.ui: User verified local Streamlit dashboard: person_down category filter shows the event; camera-1 selection retains its matching event; chatbot query 'show person down events' returns 1 matching row (screenshots supplied 2026-10-16).
1.merge: Local main checkout: only branch is main; requirements check and ingest/chatbot/event-rule/pipeline tests pass; Streamlit UI interaction was verified by user screenshot; real-video pipeline produced a SQLite event and keyframe.
1.vision: YOLO + ByteTrack on 33.2-second clip at 2 FPS: 67 sampled frames (0.0-33.0 s); primary person track ID 1 present in all 67 samples with no gaps; 1.84 detected people/sample average. Person-down labels: alerts matched 2/3 clear positive clips (first 30s clip and snow slip clip hit; icy-walk slip clip missed). Logs: data/videos/phase1_user_33s_tracks.jsonl and per-clip tracks.

2.event: Ran vision.run_pipeline on the labeled 30-second fall clip at 2 FPS on the main RTX 3050 laptop. It finished in under clip duration, wrote two person_down events to data/events.db, saved both JPEG keyframes, and generated SmolVLM captions from those frames; keyframes reviewed for event match.
2.chat: chatbot.chat.ask('Show person down events') returned all 5 stored events, including both phase2-demo and both phase2-refresh real-video events; each new event has a saved keyframe path (2026-10-16).
2.dashboard: With Auto-refresh (5 s) checked in the existing localhost:8501 dashboard, ran the labeled clip for camera phase2-refresh; the page changed from 3 to 5 events and displayed both new person_down rows and keyframes without a manual reload (2026-10-16).

3.categories: For this build, person_down is the sole kept category. Existing labeled-positive check detected 2/3 clips (first 30-second demo and snow-slip; missed icy-walk slip). README documents crowd cut from the standard detector/demo because the eight-person rule flags an ordinary queue (v006); this heuristic is now opt-in only. Fighting is cut because no classifier detects the v001/v003/v011/w001 altercation examples; tailgating/suspicious are cut because no classifier and agreed labeled test set are available. See eval/phase3_baseline.md. (2026-10-16).
3.false_alarms: Replayed 645 saved YOLO + ByteTrack frames from the reviewed 322.1-second normal shop clip through vision.run_pipeline at the configured 2 FPS into a temporary SQLite database with tuned defaults (aspect=1.2, height_drop=0.1, frames=3): 2 person_down events at 195.5 s and 300.5 s, with no crowd events. Both were visually checked and are false alerts (partial head at frame edge; standing shopper). This is below the required 3; prior defaults produced 9 on the same tracks. The 30-second demo, snowy doorway slip, and icy-walk slip also replayed through the pipeline: events in 2/3 clips. Both user-confirmed montage falls were detected. See eval/phase3_baseline.md for results and limitations (2026-10-16).
3.cameras: Replayed two supplied AVI sources sequentially through the video pipeline as camera IDs v006 and v001. After fixing camera-ID parsing, ask('Show events from camera v006') returned only its one crowd event, and ask('Show events from camera v001') returned only its two events. eval.test_chatbot now has regression coverage for nonstandard camera IDs. This verifies simulated-source filtering, not simultaneous multi-camera load (2026-10-16).
3.chat: eval.test_real_chatbot scored the fixed eval/phase3_real_chat_questions.csv against captured video-event rows, excluding the old mock; 25/25 question results matched expected category/camera/confidence/limit filters. The test works on a temporary DB copy and leaves the shared event DB unchanged (2026-10-16).
3.stability: Completed 600-second local replay of the same 30-second fall clip at 640x360 and 2 FPS with YOLO + ByteTrack, --no-vlm: pipeline exited 0 and processed through 590s without crashing, creating 21 events. Replay is a repeated scene (not varied/live footage), and processing ran faster than real time; not evidence for false-alarm performance, real-time throughput, or all-features stability (2026-10-16).

4.switches: Only semantic search is kept as an optional feature. The dashboard checkbox defaults off. eval.test_semantic used a temporary two-event DB: off returned the latest event; on used local Ollama nomic-embed-text to rank an assisted-person event first for a paraphrased query. Privacy blur and incident grouping remain unimplemented. (2026-10-16).
4.metrics: eval.phase4_vlm_ratio replayed 645 saved YOLO + ByteTrack samples from the 322.1-second normal shop clip through the pipeline in a temporary DB. It counted 2 attempted VLM calls, or 0.31% of sampled frames. Caption generation was stubbed for counting; this does not measure real VLM latency or success. (2026-10-16).
4.semantic: eval.test_semantic asked 'top 1 someone receiving assistance while prone'; the local nomic-embed-text ranking returned the event summarized as a woman kneeling on the floor while a man grabbed her arm. The ordinary latest-event result was an unrelated queue event. This is a controlled two-event fixture, not a retrieval-accuracy evaluation. (2026-10-16).
4.stability: eval.phase4_stability processed the repeated 600-second clip at 2 sampled FPS with YOLO + ByteTrack, real SmolVLM captions, keyframe saving, and a temporary event DB on the RTX 3050 A laptop GPU. It processed 1200 sampled frames in 40.8 seconds, created 2 events, saved 2 keyframes, and produced 2 real VLM captions with no fallback. Semantic search is query-time and passed separately; the clip is repeated footage, not varied/live footage. (2026-10-16).

5.accuracy: docs/phase5-evaluation.md: person_down clip-level matrix TP=2, FN=1, FP=1, TN=0; precision=66.7% and recall=66.7% on 3 reviewed positives and 1 normal clip. Same clips were used during tuning, so this is in-sample only. Chatbot check passed 25/25.
5.latency: docs/phase5-evaluation.md and eval/phase5_latency_results.json: RTX 3050 laptop, 60 sampled frames and 2 real captions; average/worst times for detect-track, VLM, JPEG, SQLite, and 25 chatbot queries. eval/phase5_dashboard_probe_results.json: 3 isolated event commits reached dashboard table DOM in average 4.776s, worst 4.977s; pixel paint not timed.
5.report: docs/phase5-evaluation.md documents the person_down confusion matrix, precision and recall, per-stage average and worst timing, and three concrete failures. The five-slide docs/phase5-review.pptx was rendered and checked slide by slide; its results and caveats agree with the report. In-sample accuracy and three-sample dashboard timing limits are explicit.
